ei.title: Chapter 4-10 3번: The Unexpected Winners of Monoculture
ei.subject: 올림포스독해의기본1

fullPassage: At one end of the spectrum of transformations was the forest gardening as practiced by the peoples of New Guinea and Amazonia that mimicked natural growth and left minimal traces on the land. At the other end was monoculture: cultivating only one species of plant or raising only one species of animal. The beginnings of monoculture can be seen in the wheat fields of the Middle East, the rice paddies of China, and the herds of sheep and goats on the Eurasian steppe. Biologically speaking, these species suddenly became very successful, measured by their rates of survival and reproduction. So did other, unwanted species. Crops that ripened or were stored after harvesting attracted rats, mice, sparrows, and roaches. Water pools provided habitats for mosquitoes. Garbage and human or animal waste attracted flies. Thanks to humans, weeds and pests were also biological winners.

questions.passage: At one end of the spectrum of transformations was the forest gardening as practiced by the peoples of New Guinea and Amazonia that (A)[mimicked / ignored] natural growth and left minimal traces on the land. At the other end was monoculture: (B)[cultivating / abandoning] only one species of plant or raising only one species of animal. The beginnings of monoculture can be seen in the wheat fields of the Middle East, the rice paddies of China, and the herds of sheep and goats on the Eurasian steppe. Biologically speaking, these species suddenly became very (C)[successful / unsuccessful], measured by their rates of survival and reproduction. So did other, unwanted species. Crops that ripened or were stored after harvesting attracted rats, mice, sparrows, and roaches. Water pools provided habitats for mosquitoes. Garbage and human or animal waste attracted flies. Thanks to humans, weeds and pests were also biological winners.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 숲 원예는 자연 성장을 모방했고(mimicked), 단일 재배는 한 종만 경작하며(cultivating), 이 종들은 매우 성공적(successful)이 되었다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① ignored — cultivating — successful (A 반대: 모방하다→무시하다)
✅ ② mimicked — cultivating — successful — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ③ mimicked — abandoning — successful (B 반대: 경작하다→포기하다)
❌ ④ mimicked — cultivating — unsuccessful (C 반대: 성공적인→실패한)

questions.passage: At one end of the spectrum of transformations was the forest gardening as practiced by the peoples of New Guinea and Amazonia that mimicked natural growth and left (A)[minimal / significant] traces on the land. At the other end was monoculture: cultivating only one species of plant or raising only one species of animal. The beginnings of monoculture can be seen in the wheat fields of the Middle East, the rice paddies of China, and the herds of sheep and goats on the Eurasian steppe. Biologically speaking, these species suddenly became very successful, measured by their rates of (B)[survival / extinction] and reproduction. So did other, unwanted species. Crops that ripened or were stored after harvesting (C)[attracted / repelled] rats, mice, sparrows, and roaches. Water pools provided habitats for mosquitoes. Garbage and human or animal waste attracted flies. Thanks to humans, weeds and pests were also biological winners.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 숲 원예는 최소한의(minimal) 흔적을 남겼고, 종의 생존율(survival)로 성공을 측정했으며, 농작물은 해충을 끌어들였다(attracted).
det.analysis:
✅ ① minimal — survival — attracted — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ② significant — survival — attracted (A 반대: 최소한의→상당한)
❌ ③ minimal — extinction — attracted (B 반대: 생존→멸종)
❌ ④ minimal — survival — repelled (C 반대: 끌어들이다→쫓아내다)

Biologically speaking, these species suddenly became very successful, measured by their rates of survival and (B)[reproduction / decline]. So did other, unwanted species. questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 변환의 스펙트럼(spectrum) 한쪽 끝에 있었고, 생존과 번식(reproduction)의 비율로 측정되었으며, 물웅덩이는 서식지(habitats)를 제공했다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① limit — reproduction — habitats (A 반대: 스펙트럼→한계)
❌ ② spectrum — decline — habitats (B 반대: 번식→쇠퇴)
✅ ③ spectrum — reproduction — habitats — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ④ spectrum — reproduction — barriers (C 반대: 서식지→장벽)

det.korean: '최대한의(maximal)'가 아니라 '최소한의(minimal)'가 문맥상 적절하다. 숲 원예는 땅에 최소한의 흔적을 남겼다.
det.analysis:
① mimicked — 모방하다, 원문 일치
② maximal — 원문은 minimal(최소한의) ←정답
③ cultivating — 경작하다, 원문 일치
④ successful — 성공적인, 원문 일치

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: '흩뿌리다(scattered)'가 아니라 '끌어들이다(attracted)'가 문맥상 적절하다. 농작물이 쥐, 생쥐, 참새, 바퀴벌레를 끌어들였다.

det.korean: '원하는(desired)'가 아니라 '원치 않는(unwanted)'이 문맥상 적절하다. 다른 원치 않는 종도 마찬가지로 성공적이었다.

questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)의 밑줄 친 see가 의미하는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 이해하다 — (B) 알아보다: (A) 발견/확인이 맞고, (B) see off는 배웅
❌ ② (A) 목격하다 — (B) 배웅하다: (A) 물리적 목격이 아닌 '확인됨'
❌ ③ (A) 확인하다 — (B) 알아보다: (B) see off는 배웅
✅ ④ (A) 확인하다 — (B) 배웅하다 ←정답

det.analysis:
❌ ① transformation(변환/변형) — 형태나 성질이 바뀌는 것, 자손 생산과 무관

✅ ② reproduction(번식/생식) — 생물이 자손을 만들어 내는 과정 ←정답

❌ ③ cultivation(경작/재배) — 땅을 일구어 작물을 기르는 것

❌ ④ harvesting(수확) — 다 자란 작물을 거두어들이는 것
det.tip: reproduction(번식): re(다시) + production(생산) = 자손을 만들어 냄

det.analysis: rates of survival and _____ 구조에서 전치사 of 뒤에 명사가 필요. survival과 병렬이므로 reproduce → reproduction.

det.analysis: _____ speaking 구조는 '~적으로 말하면'이라는 분사구문. 부사가 필요하므로 biology → biologically.

Crops that ripened or were stored after harvesting attracted rats, mice, sparrows, and roaches. Water pools provided habitats for mosquitoes. Garbage and human or animal waste attracted flies. Thanks to humans, weeds and pests were also __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 인간 덕분에 잡초와 해충도 생물학적 승자(biological winners)가 되었다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① natural predators — 천적, 잡초와 해충에 대한 서술 아님
❌ ② agricultural products — 농산물, 잡초/해충은 농산물이 아님
✅ ③ biological winners — 생물학적 승자 ←정답
❌ ④ harmful chemicals — 해로운 화학물질, 문맥상 무관
det.tip: biological winners: 인간의 활동 덕분에 생존·번식에 성공한 종을 비유적으로 표현

questions.passage: At one end of the spectrum of transformations was the forest gardening as practiced by the peoples of New Guinea and Amazonia that mimicked __________ and left minimal traces on the land. At the other end was monoculture: cultivating only one species of plant or raising only one species of animal. The beginnings of monoculture can be seen in the wheat fields of the Middle East, the rice paddies of China, and the herds of sheep and goats on the Eurasian steppe. Biologically speaking, these species suddenly became very successful, measured by their rates of survival and reproduction. So did other, unwanted species. Crops that ripened or were stored after harvesting attracted rats, mice, sparrows, and roaches. Water pools provided habitats for mosquitoes. Garbage and human or animal waste attracted flies. Thanks to humans, weeds and pests were also biological winners.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 숲 원예는 자연적 성장(natural growth)을 모방했다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① rapid expansion — 빠른 확장, 원문 표현과 불일치
❌ ② commercial farming — 상업적 농업, 숲 원예와 맞지 않음
❌ ③ artificial selection — 인위적 선택, 자연과 반대
✅ ④ natural growth — 자연적 성장 ←정답
det.tip: forest gardening은 자연의 성장 방식을 모방하여 최소한의 흔적을 남기는 농법
